question.problem:
Consider the equivalence relation $∼$ on $Z,$ defined by $x∼y$ if $5\,|\,(x-y).$ Which of the following equivalence classes contain the element $-4?$

I. $[-14]$

II. $[11]$

III. $[14]$
question.worked_solution:
We have $-4\in [x]$ if $-4∼x.$ Using the definition of the given equivalence relation, we require

$$
\begin{aligned}5\,|\,(-4-x).\end{aligned}
$$

Let's now consider each of the given equivalence classes.

- $-4\in [-14]$ because $5\,|\,(-4+14)\,✓$

- $-4\in [11]$ because $5\,|\,(-4-11)\,✓$

- $-4\notin [14]$ because $5∤(-4-14)\,\times $

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".
